subject: Archaeology

title: Sigiriya: The Lion Rock Fortress
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sigiriya: The Lion Rock Fortress usable.

hook.text: A king built his palace on top of a 600-foot rock in Sri Lanka after murdering his own father for the throne.

buildup.text: King Kashyapa I built Sigiriya around 477 CE with gardens, pools, and frescoes painted on the rock face.

discovery.text: The entrance was carved as a giant lion — visitors walked through its open jaws to reach the summit.

twist.text: When his brother returned with an army, Kashyapa rode his war elephant into a swamp and killed himself.

climax.text: The fortress became a Buddhist monastery. Monks added graffiti that is now the oldest surviving writing in Sinhalese.

punchline.text: A murdered king's fortress became a place of peace.

quiz.question: What happened to Sigiriya after King Kashyapa's death?
options: His brother demolished it completely as revenge
It became a Buddhist monastery with ancient graffiti
It was used as a military fort for the next 500 years

details.summary: Sigiriya in Sri Lanka is a massive granite rock column rising 200 meters above the jungle, topped by the ruins of a 5th-century palace built by King Kashyapa. Its elaborate water gardens, mirror wall, and frescoes of celestial maidens make it one of Asia's most remarkable archaeological sites.
details.whyItMatters: Sigiriya demonstrates sophisticated hydraulic engineering — its water gardens still function after 1,500 years. The site combines military architecture, pleasure gardens, and Buddhist monastery in a dramatic natural setting.
takeaways: A 5th-century palace built atop a 200-meter granite rock column
Features water gardens that still function after 1,500 years
Combines fortress, palace, pleasure gardens, and monastery

faq.question: Why did King Kashyapa build a palace on top of a rock?
faq.answer: Kashyapa seized the throne by killing his father and feared his exiled brother's return. The rock fortress was virtually impregnable. When his brother finally returned with an army, Kashyapa descended to fight but was defeated. After his death, the palace reverted to a Buddhist monastery.

faq.question: How did water reach the top of the rock?
faq.answer: Hydraulic engineers designed a system of cisterns, channels, and pumps that moved water up the rock face. Gravity-fed systems supplied the lower gardens. The engineering was so precise that the water gardens' fountains still operate during the rainy season using the original 5th-century plumbing.
